Cross-validated log-likelihood of normal-block models

Source: R/normal_block_cv.R
normal_block_cv.Rd

Splits the observations into folds, fits [normal_block()] on all but one fold and evaluates the held-out log-likelihood of the left-out fold (see `heldout_loglik()` in [NormalBlockBase]), for every model of the collection. It selects the number of clusters without a penalty, and compares models of different families, shapes of Sigma or scalings.

Usage

normal_block_cv(
  data,
  blocks,
  model = c("var", "mean"),
  zero_inflation = FALSE,
  sparsity = 0,
  folds = 5,
  control = NB_control(verbose = FALSE)
)

Arguments

data

a [NormalBlockData] object

blocks

as in [normal_block()]: a range of numbers of clusters, a single one, or a known clustering (p x q indicator matrix)

model, zero_inflation, sparsity

as in [normal_block()]. A sparsity path (`sparsity = TRUE`) is not supported: its penalty grid depends on the data, hence on the fold; pick the penalty with StARS instead (see [NormalBlockVarCollectionSparsity]).

folds

the number of folds, or a vector of `data$n` fold labels. With a number, the folds are drawn at random, stratified on the distinct rows of the design X when it is categorical (e.g. a factor coded by `model.matrix()`), so that every training set sees every category.

control

a list of controls, see [NB_control()]

Value

an object of class `normal_block_cv`: a data frame with one row per model (`q`), the total held-out log-likelihood over the `n` observations (`loglik`, larger is better) and its standard error (`se`, from the spread of the per-observation values); the per-observation values are kept in the `per_observation` attribute (n x number of models) and the folds in `folds`. Its `best` attribute is the q chosen by the one-standard-error rule, the smallest q within one standard error of the maximum; `best_max` is the maximum itself, which tends to over-select.

Examples

ex   <- generate_normal_block_var_data(n = 60, p = 15, d = 1, q = 3)
data <- NormalBlockData$new(ex$Y, ex$X)
set.seed(1)
cv <- normal_block_cv(data, blocks = 2:4, folds = 3)
cv
#> Cross-validated log-likelihood, 3 folds (larger is better)
#>  q    loglik       se
#>  2 -1640.221 32.06930
#>  3 -1598.375 29.03992
#>  4 -1582.373 28.29224
#> Best: q = 3 (one-standard-error rule; maximum at q = 4)
